children.text: Osteoid Osteomas are small, benign, osteogenic bone lesions most commonly found in the proximal femur. Patients typically present between ages 5 and 25 with regional pain that is worse at night and improves with NSAIDs.
Diagnosis is made radiographically by a characteristic lesion that is less than 1.5 cm in diameter with a sclerotic margin and radiolucent nidus.
High resolution CT scan distinguishes osteoid osteomas from other radiolucent bone lesions
Treatment is usually nonoperative with observation and NSAID for pain control. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) or surgical resection may be indicated in patients with progressive and severe symptoms.
